assumptions: The rollout population responds as the tested sample did.
final.diagnosis: The test measured a lift of 3.24% and a net of Rs.10.55 per treated customer.
final.rationale: scale: P(net>0)=1.00 >= 0.80 and 5th percentile Rs.138,937 above the tolerable loss of Rs.-2,400. Funded at 14,313 customers, the rollout is projected to earn Rs.151,004 net of Rs.99,413 in incentives.

assumptions: The expected lift is the model's hypothesis, not a measurement.
Break-even assumes the incentive is redeemed on every treated order.
initial.diagnosis: Baseline conversion is 8.0%. This promotion needs a lift of 1.00% before it breaks even, because the incentive is charged on every treated order, not only the extra ones.
initial.rationale: The economics can work: at the proposed lift this earns Rs.384,000 net. But the confidence rests on history, not on a measurement on this merchant, so the honest next step is a controlled test of 2,963 customers per arm at a cost of Rs.19,556. Rollout stays closed until that test clears the scaling rule.
